subject: Customer request: cash liability & termination rights in SLA
messages:

Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA — request for cash liability and termination rights

Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we discussed with the procurement and legal teams, NovaMed runs regulated production workloads and our risk tolerance for downtime is low. The standard credits-only remedy in the draft doesn't meet our internal controls.

Specifically, we need:
- Fee-at-risk / liquidated damages: 20% of monthly committed spend held as a recoverable pool for SLA violations (or an equivalent per-hour LD schedule).
- Termination right: ability to terminate for convenience with a buyout if Redwood has two severity-1 outages >4 hours within a 90-day window.
- No limitations on cumulative damages beyond credits.

I've attached a short write-up with the redlines from our side (NovaMed_SLA_asks_03082027.pdf). Procurement is asking for a written confirmation that Redwood can absorb cash liability — this will be a gating item for our CFO sign-off.

Please route to legal and let me know when you can provide a concrete response.

Best,
Carlos

Carlos — thanks for the clear note and for sharing the redlines. Looping in Priyom (legal) and Rishi (ops) to get us a defensible position quickly.

High-level thoughts from me: we want NovaMed on Redwood for the long term and we take uptime seriously, but we typically avoid uncapped liquidated damages in exchange for structured remedies. Two alternatives we can move on quickly:

1) Cash reserve/escrow: hold a small percentage of the first-year committed spend in an escrow account for SLA-related make-whole payments.
2) Tiered termination: allow termination only after repeated, qualifying outages (with cure periods and an agreed remediation plan), rather than a single event.

Can Priyom and Rishi outline a concrete counterproposal we can put in writing? Happy to set a 30-minute sync this week with procurement/legal.

Thanks — Marissa

Marissa / team — quick legal POV and proposed counterlanguage.

We are comfortable discussing a limited cash-backed remedy for enterprise commitments, but we must tightly scope it to:
- A cap (expressed as % of committed spend or a fixed dollar cap).
- A clear trigger set (specific SLOs with measurement method, severity definitions, and monitoring windows).
- Cure periods and remediation obligations before termination is permitted.

Proposed counter (draft language we can share for redline):
- Credits remain the primary remedy: formula = ((target uptime - measured uptime) / target uptime) * monthly fees, up to a 50% monthly credit cap.
- Cash reserve: 5% of first-year committed spend held in custodial escrow for 12 months; can be used only for qualified SLA make-whole payments. Any unused portion returns to Redwood at end of term.
- Termination: Customer may terminate for material SLA failure only after (a) two qualifying monthly SLA misses in a rolling 6-month period, or (b) a single P1 incident >6 hours that is attributable to Redwood where Redwood fails to cure within 30 days and provide a root-cause/remediation plan.
- Liquidated damages per-hour schedules will not be accepted as a first resort; they are disproportionately punitive for shared infra and would materially increase price for other customers.

If NovaMed confirms committed spend (ARR) and target SLOs, we can convert % proposals to hard-dollar numbers for procurement. I'll attach a redline with suggested wording.

– Priyom
Priyom Das | Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Quick ops note from my side:
- For Hosted customers on our standard stack, 99.9% monthly is a realistic target. For Dedicated customers (reserved GPU pools) we can operate at 99.99% with the right capacity and redundancy.
- Measured SLOs must exclude planned maintenance windows and customer-caused issues.
- We cannot support an open-ended per-hour LD schedule tied to total downtime without a big price uplift — the engineering and capacity model changes materially.

Practical counterproposal we can delivery-engineer:
- Escrow option for enterprise: 7% of first-year committed spend for Dedicated customers (custodial, returns unused balance).
- Termination only after either (i) two qualifying months below 99.5% within 6 months, or (ii) a single P1 >6 hours attributable to Redwood with failed cure.
- One-time cash make-whole cap = 25% of quarterly committed fee (prevents open-ended liability).

I'll attach our SLO benchmark export so procurement can see historical distributions. If NovaMed wants lower caps or quicker termination triggers, we need to price that into the committed spend.

– Rishi
Rishi Malhotra | Head of Product Ops | Redwood Inference

Marissa / Priyom / Rishi — thanks for the quick turnaround. Procurement has reviewed and we remain firm on a couple of points:
- The 7% escrow and 25% cap are a start but do not replace a per-hour LD schedule we can present to the CFO. We need a mechanism that maps directly to business impact (we've provided a sample $/hour matrix in the attachment).
- Termination after one P1 >4 hours is a hard requirement for our internal risk policy. Two incidents in 90 days is not acceptable.

If Redwood cannot accept those terms, procurement will escalate to our CFO and consider alternate vendors that can provide cash-backed LDs.

We can hop on an executive call — please propose times; we prefer this week.

Carlos

Carlos — I appreciate the clarity and the timeline. We want to avoid a full procurement escalation if possible, so here's a path I can propose to both sides this week:

1) Executive review: 30–45 minute call between NovaMed CIO/CFO and my director (cc'd on scheduling separately) to walk the tradeoffs and economic impact.
2) Compromise proposal (written):
   - Custodial escrow = 7% of first-year committed spend (Dedicated-only offering), refundable after 12 months except for qualified SLA make-whole payments.
   - Termination: allowed after either (a) two qualifying months below 99.5% in a 6-month rolling window, OR (b) a single P1 outage >6 hours attributable to Redwood where Redwood fails to provide documented remediation within 30 days. (We will not accept a single P1 >4h as an automatic termination trigger without price adjustment.)
   - One-time make-whole cash cap = 25% of quarterly committed fee.
3) Operational commitments: increased monitoring, a dedicated runbook for NovaMed, and a named ops escalation contact.

If NovaMed accepts the above as a negotiated compromise I will get Priyom to convert it into redline language for signature. If you still require the per-hour LD schedule and single-event termination without any price uplift, we understand that will need to go to executive review and potential procurement escalation.

Proposed times for the exec call: Thu 11:00–11:45 or Fri 09:00–09:45 PT. Which works for you?

Regards,
